la:verb:alo.gloss: to feed, to nourish, to nurture
senses: to feed, to nourish, to nurture
to cultivate, to raise, to rear, etc. (as a child, an animal, etc.)
to cause (a thing) to continue over time: to further, to maintain, to sustain
to encourage or promote the development (of a thing): to foster, to further, to promote (something)
la:verb:alo.html:
ălo, ălŭi, altum, and ălĭtum, 3, v. a. (the ante-class. and class. form of the
part. perf. from Plautus until after Livy is altus (in Cic. four times); alitus seems to have been first used in the post-Aug. per. to distinguish it from altus, the adj. Altus is found in ; Varr. ap. ; ; ; ; ; ; on the contrary, alitus,; ; ; ; ; 9, 3, 8; , praef. 10; ; ; cf. ; ; P.; ) [cf.: ἄν-αλτος = insatiable, ἄλσος = growth (of wood), 1. ad-oleo, ad-olesco, elementum; Goth. alan = to bring up; Germ. alt = old; Engl. old, eld, elder, and alderman], to feed, to nourish, support, sustain, maintain (in gen. without designating the means, while nutrire denotes sustenance by animal food; cf. Herz. ad ; ; Doed. Syn. II. p. 99).
Lit.: quem ego nefrendem alui, Liv. And. ap. Fest. s. v. nefrendes, p. 163 Müll. (Trag. Rel. p. 5 Rib.): Athenis natus altusque,: alebat eos,: esurientes alebat,.—With natus, educatus, or a similar word, several times: Alui, educavi, Att. ap. (Trag. Rel. p. 150 Rib.): cum Hannibale alto atque educato inter arma, (cf. II. infra): aut equos Alere aut canes ad venandum,; : alere nolunt hominem edacem,: quoniam cibus auget corpus alitque,; : quae etiam aleret adulescentes,: milites,: nautas,: exercitum,: magnum numerum equitatus,: cum agellus eum non satis aleret,; so : locus ille, ubi altus aut doctus est,: quibus animantes aluntur,: (animus) aletur et sustentabitur isdem rebus, quibus astra sustentantur et aluntur, al.: latrociniis se suosque alebat,; : quos manus aut lingua perjurio aut sanguine civili alebat,; cf. Kritz ad ; : ut nepotem elephantos alere prohiberet,: canes,: quod alerentur regiones eorum ab illo,: velut amnis imbres Quem super notas aluere ripas,have swollen,: rhombos aequora alebant,; ; ; and in a paradoxical phrase: infelix minuendo corpus alebat, and sustained his body by consuming it, i. e. nourished himself by his own flesh, al.—Hence in pass. with the abl. = vesci, to be nourished or sustained with or by something, to live or feed upon: panico vetere atque hordeo corrupto omnes alebantur,: quia viperinis carnibus alantur,: locustis eos ali, etc.,: hoc cibo aliti sunt,.—
Fig., to nourish, cherish, promote, increase, strengthen: honos alit artes,: in eā ipsā urbe, in quā et nata et alta sit eloquentia,: hominis mens alitur discendo et cogitando,: haec studia adulescentiam alunt,; cf. Ochsn. Eclog. 134 al.: civitas, quam ipse semper aluisset,i. e. whose prosperity he had always promoted,: vires,: nolo meis impensis illorum ali augerique luxuriam,: alere morbum,: insita hominibus libido alendi de industriā rumores,: regina Vulnus alit venis,: divitiis alitur luxuriosus amor,: alitur diutius controversia,: quid alat formetque poëtam,—Hence, altus, a, um.
la:verb:alo.inflection: ălŭi, altum, and ălĭtum, 3, v. a., adj.
